title: Small cleanup in auth error handlers
bug: 401/403 responses rename the `message` field to `name`, unlike every other error.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions 'tidy' and 'cleanup' with no announcement of renaming the response field from 'message' to 'name', which changes the API contract for all auth error responses.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions 'tidy' and 'cleanup' with no announcement of renaming the response field from 'message' to 'name', which changes the API contract for all auth error responses.

findings.label: regression

doppel_guided.summary: The PR silently renames the 'message' field to 'name' in authentication error responses, breaking API compatibility without announcement.

suspicions.claim: Authentication error responses now return 'name' instead of 'message', breaking the documented error format and existing clients.
suspicions.trigger: Send a request without Authorization header (or with invalid token). Read response JSON: expect {'code': 401, 'message': 'Unauthorized', 'description': '...'} but will get {'code': 401, 'name': 'Unauthorized', 'description': '...'}.
suspicions.evidence: No probe sent a request without Authorization header or with invalid token to GET /api/users or any protected endpoint; all requests succeeded with 200 responses.

suspicions.claim: Basic auth error handler (used by POST /api/tokens) returns 'name' instead of 'message' and includes a 'WWW-Authenticate' header that token auth handler does not, creating inconsistent error shapes between the two auth flows.
suspicions.trigger: Send request with invalid Basic auth credentials (wrong username/password). Read response JSON and headers: body will have 'name' not 'message'; response includes header 'WWW-Authenticate: Form'.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe-s2: POST /api/tokens changed: message (removed), name (added)

suspicions.claim: Token auth error handler (used by all other /api/* endpoints) returns 'name' instead of 'message' and omits the 'WWW-Authenticate' header, so clients that rely on that header for basic auth challenges will not see it on token auth failures.
suspicions.trigger: Send request with expired or invalid Bearer token. Read response JSON and headers: body has 'name' not 'message'; no 'WWW-Authenticate' header present.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe-s3: GET /api/users changed: message (removed), name (added)
